Cc: ProcureOps Integrations <procureops+ops@procureops.io>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Multi-portal decommission / SIG rehome request

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from NovaHealth security: our procurement team is consolidating vendor portals and has asked us to present a single, authoritative SIG/CAIQ profile for Redwood by 2028-01-10. Right now our evidence is split across Whistic and Vendr (both have different attachments and Q&A fragments).

Can Redwood: 
- Propose a minimal migration plan to rehome our SIG to one portal (we'd prefer Vendr as canonical),
- Confirm what evidence you will copy vs. reference (we want to avoid duplicating sensitive logs), and
- Share any temporary permissions or object locations you need for a secure transfer.

Attached: nova_SIG_export_20271213.json (current SIG export).

We'd like a quick 30-minute call to lock the timeline — availability: Thu 12/16 or Fri 12/17 morning PST.

Thanks,
Maya Patel
Security Operations Manager
NovaHealth

--

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <security@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Multi-portal decommission / SIG rehome request

Maya — thanks for the context and the export. We can take the lead on consolidating the authoritative SIG into Vendr and decommissioning the duplicate Whistic profile, subject to a quick verification step. High-level plan below; happy to walk through live.

Planned approach (draft):
1) Inventory & mapping (48h): Marcus will run a diff between the Whistic and Vendr profiles and produce a small manifest of unique fragments / attachments.
2) Evidence policy decision (you & NovaHealth): mark items as COPY vs REFERENCE vs SENSITIVE-REFERENCE (we will reference the S3 location and not store copies in the portal).
3) Secure transfer (1–2 business days once policy agreed): if items are to be copied, we'll ingest into Vendr via secure S3 presigned URLs and record provenance in the SIG metadata.
4) Validation & signoff (1 day): Kimberly will run a QA pass on the migrated profile against the export you shared; you confirm final handoff.
5) Whistic decommission (target date after signoff): update Whistic status to archived and add a pointer to Vendr as the canonical source.

Permissions / information we need from NovaHealth:
- Confirm preferred canonical portal (Vendr OK?)
- The S3 prefix or a short-term presigned URL for any logs you do not want copied
- Any data retention/expiration constraints we should encode

I attached our internal checklist to this reply so you can see concrete steps. If Thu 12/16 10:00–10:30 PST works, we'll send a calendar invite.

Attachments: redwood_portal_migration_checklist.pdf

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Security Programs Lead
Redwood Inference

Thanks Jonas — Vendr as canonical is fine with us. We reviewed the checklist and have the following notes: 

- Anything marked SENSITIVE-REFERENCE: we will provide a time-limited S3 presigned URL (12 hours) rather than copies.
- Retention: NovaHealth requires PII-related logs to be retained for 90 days and then redacted. Please document how references to those artifacts will be handled in the SIG metadata.
- Audit window: procurement confirms they can accept the consolidated Vendr profile if we have signoff by 2028-01-05 to allow final review before 1/10.

We are available Thu 12/16 10:00 PST for the call.

Best,
Maya
